restrictions: The two messages have 60 and 62 bytes: each is one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and its true block length; the 62-byte message ends in two zero bytes.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every choice of nine state words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7, and a second exact construction enumerates such pairs with the round-1 state word Y4 held inside a class of 4,096 values. Heuristic part: a search over 2^115 such pairs, all with Y4 in the class, for one whose remaining 128 digest bits agree.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; seven trials per 256-bit word in 36-bit lanes on a 16-register load/store machine; a batch is 154 operations (arithmetic, logical and shift operations, two comparisons and two branches) plus 74 loads and is charged, together with the per-alpha setup and the last partial batch of every class loop, as 34 per trial; no sorting or lookup and no table that grows with the number of trials (two fixed lists of 586 words hold the class members and are read in order); at most 2^104 early-test passes are processed before the algorithm halts with failure.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word. The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1 and H2. The factor 4,096 in H1 is assumed and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments; it is justified only by the disclosed joint estimator, whose three-standard-error lower bound is 4,871 (estimate 7,319, standard error 816, class e96d6d6b, three betas, 2^41 draws per beta, fresh seed after all selections). With the uniform rate instead, the same search needs 2^127 trials and gives time_log2 123.4; at the previously assumed 2,048 the same construction with X12 < 2^8 gives time_log2 112.4 (the fallback). No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed.

Six 32-bit constants and the 32-bit word eta that defines the class are stored in the program (28 bytes of advice); they were selected by participant measurements, the constants as the best of 4,140 candidate sets and the class among the classes seen in the samples, and recomputing the constants and selecting them and eta is bounded by 2^63 units and included in the time. No priority or novelty claim is made; the number of trials is 2^115 instead of 2^128 because a trial is assumed to succeed 4,096 times more often than a uniform 128-bit value would.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the 2^115 enumerated trials behave with respect to the event that the 128-bit residual R is zero like independent events of probability at least 2^-116 each (4,096 times the rate of a uniform 128-bit value), to the extent that the probability that no trial has R = 0 is at most exp(-1/2) + 0.002.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 6.4: lengths 60 and 62, the six constants of Section 3.2, the class of Y4 defined by eta = e96d6d6b (Lemma Q), contexts indexed by (X12, X13, X14) with X12 < 2^7, the D0 family with parameter alpha, and all 4,096 members of the class for every context and alpha.
heuristics.extrapolation: From a participant estimate of the class rate, that is of the number of solutions with Y4 in the class of the seven-word system that determines R, obtained by sampling one of the two calls involved and counting the other call for each sample: a lower bound of 7,319 times the uniform expectation with standard error 816, from 2^41 draws for each of three values of an auxiliary difference, drawn with a new seed after the constants, the class and those three values were fixed; its three-standard-error lower bound is 4,871 > 4,096. The same package's eight further seeds give sums between 5,946 and 7,785, mean 7,003 with standard error of the mean 241, whose three-standard-error lower bound 6,280 also exceeds 4,096 and whose smallest sum 5,946 exceeds it by 1.45x. The count per sample is exact where the enumeration fits a work budget and a random-subset estimate otherwise. In the quoted run 5,388 samples were counted: all 417 nonzero values are counts made in full, and the random-subset branch was used only for 915 samples, each with the estimate zero, of which 80 drawn at random were confirmed to have no solution by a SAT solver. Of the 417 nonzero counts, 100 were given to an independent model counter, which counted all of them: for the 40 largest, which carry 45.6% of the sum, the ratio of sums is 1.027, and for 60 drawn at random it is 0.969. The preceding pass of the same size, in which this class was the largest of eight and which is therefore biased upwards, gave 7,173 with standard error 778. All of this is in proof.md Section 10. The extrapolation is from these to the rate of R = 0 over 2^115 real trials.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 4,096 is assumed. It is set against a participant estimate, a lower bound of 7,319 with standard error 816 whose three-standard-error lower bound is 4,871, which the organizer-run experiments do not measure; the success bound needs a factor of at least 4,090. With factor 1 (the uniform rate) the claim would be 2^127 trials and time_log2 123.4; with factor 2,048, the previously disclosed assumption on this track, the same construction halved in breadth (X12 < 2^8, 2^116 trials) prices at time_log2 112.4, and this package falls back to that claim if the 4,096 premise is declined. The margin between the assumed 4,096 and the three-standard-error bound 4,871 is 1.19x; the previous package assumed 2,048 against the same 4,871, a margin of 2.38x: this package halves the evidence margin to halve the search. The class rate is a heavy-tailed quantity, a sum of counts of very different sizes with 84% of it from one auxiliary difference. Two smaller passes for this class scattered far more than their standard errors suggest (9,472 with standard error 4,793 from 10 nonzero values, then 2,404 with standard error 831 from 13); only the passes with 2^41 draws are relied on (the second, the third and eight further seeds, ten sums between 5,946 and 7,785), and the assumed 4,096 is 1.71 times below the eight-seed mean and 1.45 times below the smallest seed. The six constants (best of 4,140 candidate sets) and the class were selected by participant measurements of this kind, and the largest of many noisy estimates is biased upwards: only the third-pass figure 7,319 and the eight further seeds were obtained on fresh draws after the constants, the class and its auxiliary differences were fixed. The counting program is the participant's, and so is every check of it. The 417 nonzero values behind the 7,319 are counts made in full; the independent counter confirmed 100 of them and was not given the other 317. How often the random-subset branch was used in the other passes and for the other classes was not examined, and brute force confirms the program only for 8-bit words, where that branch cannot be reached. The model that six of the seven words behave like independent uniform words is tested on real messages only for events of probability about 2^-32 and above, and end to end only at 8-bit and 10-bit words; its use at 2^-116 cannot be tested directly. At 32 bits two statistics of the runs with shared seed words are 2.3 and 2.1 standard deviations from the model, and other comparisons showed 2.6, 2.7 and 3.1, with one pair statistic 3.1 twice in opposite directions: a spread between runs larger than a Poisson count allows, which bears on independence and is under study. Trial independence is assumed: all trials of a run share the four seed words and the 4,096 trials of one context and alpha differ only in Y4 and what follows. The present package changes only the score-critical premise (2,048 -> 4,096) and the breadth of the context loop (X12 < 2^8 -> 2^7); it reuses the predecessor's estimator campaign unchanged and adds no new measurement; 4,096 is exactly the multiple that puts 2^127/f trials on the 2^115 the halved loop supplies. Nothing here is organizer-verified except the two declared experiments, which do not measure the 128-bit rate and are not a test of H1.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.999 over the random word, fewer than 2^104 of the 2^115 trials pass the 32-bit early test of proof.md Lemma E without having R = 0.
heuristics.scope: The early test of Section 6.3 on the trials of Section 6.4. The measured pass rate 2^-29.6 would give 2^85.4 passes; the budget of 2^104 corresponds to a pass rate of 2^-11 and is larger by a factor of about 2^18.6, and processing 2^104 passes is charged in the time bound (2^114 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: From participant measurements of the pass rate on real trials of the class search at 32 bits (5,498 passes in 2^42 trials with an independent random context per thread; 1,319 passes in eight runs of 2^37 trials with seed words shared by all contexts of a run, between 150 and 177 per run; 2^42 draws of the seven-word model gave 5,463; all in proof.md Section 10) to the 2^115 trials of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The measured rate is a mean; that the pass count of a full run of 2^115 trials, whose contexts share the four seed words, stays near that mean is assumed. Eight runs of 2^37 trials are the only test of a shared-seed layout at 32 bits, and in them the state word S5, which the algorithm holds fixed over a run, was not shared. The budget exceeds the passes expected at the measured rate by a factor of about 2^18.6. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H2 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.001.
